title: [Suite autour de Teichmüller dont] Teichmülleries, 1981-1982 : notes manuscrites (1981-1983, s.d.), lettres (1981, s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
This page is the verso, or a handwritten continuation, of a typed letter to 'Shurik' (Grothendieck) signed 'Barry', almost certainly Barry Mazur. The typed side is visible as mirror-image bleed-through. The previous page gives Mazur's typed answers to questions Grothendieck had sent him in 1981:
(a) Does an extension of a finite group by a contractible group split? No. Deligne's counterexample pushes out a Heisenberg-type extension 1→Z→H→Z/3×Z/3→1 along Z = center of the universal cover of SL_2(R).
(b) Can a contractible group have torsion? No for Lie groups; otherwise unknown.
(c) A 'cone' question about fixed-point sets of involutions of B^3. Answered negatively with a Bing-type wild example.
(d) Finite subgroups of the Teichmüller group, 'related to recent work of Thurston'.

The handwritten addition reports a check with Siebenmann and 'Kravitz' (very probably Saul Kravetz):
(1) It is 'unknown' whether every finite subgroup Γ of the Teichmüller (mapping class) group Γ_g is realized by automorphisms of an algebraic curve. This is the Nielsen realization problem, equivalently whether Γ has a fixed point in Teichmüller space T_g.
(2) It is true for finite solvable Γ.
(3) It is true for genus 2.

A final paragraph concerns a hypersurface Y ⊂ X and a finite-order automorphism (Z/n) of X that is the identity on Y. Siebenmann says this is 'certainly solvable using Smith theory (i.e. n=1)'. This presumably means a periodic map fixing a codimension-one submanifold pointwise is forced to be trivial, given the implicit hypotheses (e.g. side-preserving / orientation conditions; otherwise a reflection with n=2 occurs). This is via Smith theory: fixed sets of Z/p actions are mod-p homology manifolds, and codimension-one fixed sets force local orientation reversal (Newman-type rigidity).

The problem served is Grothendieck's 'Teichmüller tower' programme. Torsion in Teichmüller groups and its realization by curves with automorphisms is exactly what is needed to relate the discrete Teichmüller groupoids to the stack M_{g,n}: stabilizers of points equal automorphism groups of curves. The topological questions (contractible groups with torsion, fixed points on cells/cones) are the 'Smith theory' side of 'finite group acting on a contractible space T_g has a fixed point'.
errors: Statement (1) was already outdated in 1981. Kerckhoff had announced the solution of the Nielsen realization problem (every finite subgroup of the mapping class group fixes a point of Teichmüller space) in Bull. AMS 1980, with the full paper in Annals 1983, using Thurston's earthquakes. This is consistent with the previous page's allusion to 'recent work of Thurston'.
The informant 'Kravitz' is likely Saul Kravetz. His 1959 claimed proof of Nielsen realization was known to be flawed, which may explain the 'unknown' status he reported.
Final paragraph: the condition must be 'identity on Y', not 'identity on X'. Also 'n=1' only follows under extra hypotheses (side/orientation preserving); a reflection gives n=2.

ideas.what: Realizability of finite subgroups of the Teichmüller group as automorphism groups of curves (fixed points of finite groups on T_g)
ideas.where_published: Possibly alluded to in Esquisse d'un programme's discussion of torsion in Teichmüller groups (unsure)

ideas.modern_name: Fenchel's theorem (Nielsen realization for solvable groups)
Nielsen realization in genus 2 (hyperelliptic involution, explicit classification)

ideas.what: Finite-order automorphism fixing a hypersurface pointwise is trivial (or a reflection), via Smith theory
ideas.modern_name: Smith theory / Newman's theorem on periodic maps
ideas.usually_credited_to: P. A. Smith; M. H. A. Newman

missed.claim: Historical documentation: in 1981 Grothendieck, via Mazur, Siebenmann and Deligne, was actively seeking whether finite subgroups of Teichmüller groups are realized by curve automorphisms (Nielsen realization). This is a key input for identifying the Teichmüller groupoid tower with the stack of curves. He received outdated information ('unknown') even though Kerckhoff's announcement was already out.

missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It documents the information sources and the state of knowledge behind the Teichmüller-tower part of Esquisse d'un programme. This is only of historical interest, not a new mathematical result.

deep.surprise_reason: The page is a correspondent's (Mazur's) relay of standard, partly outdated facts about Nielsen realization and a Smith-theory remark. There is no new mathematics by Grothendieck, only historical context for his Teichmüller programme.
transcription_corrections: 'Kravitz' is probably Saul Kravetz, the Teichmüller-space author of the 1959 claimed Nielsen realization proof.
'which is identity on X' should read 'identity on Y'.
'finite solvable gp[-s-]. +' is a hand correction; the intended reading is 'finite solvable gps.'
